verdicts.kill_A: The Tsebelis (1989) mixed-equilibrium prediction is a classical textbook result in game theory. Testing it in LLM agents is a straightforward 'Homo silicus' application (Horton, arXiv:2301.07543)—replicating another well-known economics experiment with LLM subjects—with no conceptual novelty in the mechanism beyond standard mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium, and prior work (Lorè & Heydari; Duan et al.; Akata et al.) already shows LLMs deviate from equilibrium predictions.
verdicts.kill_B: Okamoto et al. (arXiv:2608.12323, AIES 2026) already demonstrated the penalty paradox in LLMs—small fines lowering compliance across 12 models. The U-shaped curve is merely the standard Gneezy & Rustichini (2000) crowding-out pattern with a large-fine deterrence arm trivially expected from Becker (1968), and the flat-monitor claim is a trivial no-feedback consequence. This is a replication of already-published LLM behavior plus a textbook human result.
